kurz: [[pektin|Pectin]] from fruit forms a gel, but only with enough sugar and acid. That is why jam needs both.
bild_im_kopf: Like a lock with three keys: pectin, sugar and acid. If one is missing, it stays runny.
was_passiert: Pectins are long chains from fruit cell walls. [[zucker|Sugar]] draws water away from them, and [[saeure|acid]] takes away the charge that makes them repel each other. Then they can link into a network. Apples, quinces and redcurrants have a lot of pectin, strawberries little.
warum_wichtig: Explains why jam with little sugar does not set and why lemon juice belongs in it.
faustregeln: Setting test: a dollop on a cold plate should form a skin after a minute.
Combine low-pectin fruit with apples or jam sugar.
Lemon juice helps with mild fruit.
